The humid marshland air nearly vibrates with the incessant droning of insects. With each step the Traveler takes further from the drier fields they left 
behind, they sink deeper into the sodden soil, the smells of loamy rot erupting to assail the senses as mud squishes and pulls. All the while, along the 
distant horizon, a green smudge of the Wealdwoods promises dry firm earth and cover from the oppressive sun above.
As the Traveler pushes aside stalks of cattail to step onto a knoll of mossy stone, they are met with silence from the interrupted mating croaks of amphibians. 
With only the sound of buzzing insects, the Traveler grips their coral walking stick tightly in their fist, way of the unnerving quiet. Mere heartbeats later, 
an eruption of silty water explodes along the water's edge, surprising the Traveler as a gray skinned amphibian with tentacles whipping from its open 
mouth hops towards them, quickly closing the distance. The Traveler sees the yellow viscid fluid splash off the tentacles of the rushing glomunder and 
knows they are in for a dangerous encounter. Before the Traveler can raise their staff to strike, a pink and bone white spear darts in from the unsettled 
water and the gray amphibian crashes hard onto the stone, a massive tongue breaching its side.
The Traveler stands stunned and unexpectedly grateful as they watch the head of a solmundis rise from the water and drag their prey back into the water, 
its hooked tongue stuck firm between the poor glomunder's ribs while its struggling kicks slowly lose strength. With a sigh of relief, the Traveler wipes 
sweat from their brow and begins looking for a sharp stone to affix onto their staff, a spear suddenly sounding like a good idea.
The Life Blood of Sol’Kesh
From torrential flooded rivers, to stagnant peat bogs, countless 
creatures have adapted to freshwater environments to make 
the most out of the mercurial existence. Many fish developed 
rudimentary lungs or the means to leave the water when needed. 
Birds migrate in great numbers to take advantage of both 
blossoming new life and the bleak final days of fish fighting for 
the last ounce of water in a drying lake bottom. Arthropods of all 
sorts crawl and fly in endless numbers, the humid air allowing 
them to grow large quickly. Many mammals, both aquatic and 
terrestrial, can be found wallowing in the same waters for untold 
generations, while others migrate, feasting on the fish and plants 
that flourish when the season is right. But no class of creature has 
benefited more than the amphibians that thrive in this crossroads 
of aquatic and terrestrial existence, thriving in the mud unlike 
any other, and so it is of no surprise that amphibians have come 
to dominate this biome as the largest of them, reigns unopposed 
in the murky depths. 
Stepping into Mire and Muck
These wetlands are unsuspectingly lethal; a calm gentle river 
can transform into a raging white water rapids, a peaceful still 
lake with its mirror-fine surface may harbor fathomless depths 
and unseen predators, and the mud of endless marshlands can 
consume the body of any unsure of their step. For those able to 
find means to stay dry or traverse the water safely, they can find 
bountiful fishing spots, amphibians to catch and thousands of 
plants to harvest. Though the trip rarely takes the same path twice 
as the terrain can change within the span of a single rainstorm.
The Fenlands are one with the changes of weather and seasons, a 
Traveler must not only be aware of what flora and fauna dwell in 
the area, they must also know if recent rains have swollen the once 
calm river to a torrential rapid, whether the watering hole that 
supplies whole herds with life has dried, or how deep a lake might 
be in case a colossal predator resides within its black depths. 
As these waters run through all of Sol’Kesh, the Fenlands are not 
always a destination to find, but a constant in every environment. 
A Traveler must always keep a wary eye out for what lies in the 
mud and deep waters, and carry a fishing rod in hand to make the 
best of it.
North of the Inmere, above tall cliffs rests a gray solemn moor that stretches to the Thornfen woods. This pock-marked marsh can 
hardly support trees in its alkaline waters, instead growing undulating wet dross grass and bog petals that leave vast expanses of soggy 
grounds. Beneath these thick grasses drains a slurry of swamp water down to the Undermoor caves below, along with many discarded 
husks and bones to moulder in the caverns. Under these obscure waters, murrow thrive, blindly navigating the twisting sinkholes and 
swallowing whole any that wade into their waters. Fortunately too large for the voracious murrow, herds of baughur wallow above, 
munching on the drab plant life that manages to rise from the algae choked waters in this forebodingly dank expanse.

The Sinking Horizon
Unlike the older salamanders, the solmundis 
young spend less time hiding in the mud, and are 
instead found swimming and wrestling with their 
clutch mates. This behavior, while unsafe, aids the 
amphibians in weeding out the weak and unwary 
from the numerous predators that prowl the 
Fenlands.
While still small, the young solmundis’ wickedly 
sharp tongue is nearly adult sized. At first they are 
highly inaccurate, but with their formative month 
of practice, trying to harpoon fish and crab, those 
that can eat their fill, survive and improve upon 
their lethal aim
